rulings.why: Real: the adjustment worsens the wearer’s armor check penalty by 2 and no armor-delta field exists, so a situational star is the only honest lane — but the judge’s wording calls a check PENALTY an 'untyped bonus' and drops the Strength-entry condition the same item changes; fix reworded.

situational.when: wearing armor fitted with twining chains — its armor check penalty is 2 worse, and its Strength entry is 2 higher so you meet it less often

rulings.why: Overturned: a relic ASPECT, not an ownable item (level 0, no price, no invested trait — build.ts only reads item.innateSpells for INVESTED inventory), and atWill over-grants a 1d4-round-recharge activation into unlimited casting while silently discarding the printed 6th rank (InnateSpellGrant ignores  when atWill is set).

Real granted Strike on an invested implant, but the judge wrongly claimed grantedStrikes has no range key — GrantedStrike.range exists (spined-azarketi, venom-spit), so the fix as written turns a ranged spray into a melee attack.

Real: neither the sanctuary casting nor any use limit is on the record. But limitedUses is a FEAT field — ItemBase has no such key; the item lane for 'five per day' is frequency, which itemUses.ts synthesizes into a counter chip.

Overturned: the text worsens the MULTIPLE ATTACK PENALTY, not the attack roll — a strikeAttack star reading '-1 untyped' misstates the first attack of every turn; and the siphon is isAttachable (usage attached-to-melee-weapon), so once affixed its inv entry carries attachedTo and InventoryTab hides every carry-flag control, leaving explain.ts’s equipped/worn/invested gate permanently unsatisfiable.

Real encumbrance relief, but ignoredBulk alone is dead: derive.ts makeEffBulk reads it only when item.itemType === 'container' (all 46 shipped ignoredBulk items are containers, none otherwise). Capacity is left unset — the printed text names none and InventoryTab treats absent capacity as no limit.
Upheld: the stored text prints a standing Speed change and the fix reproduces items.supramarine-chair’s passiveEffects.speeds formula verbatim — verified character-for-character against core.json.

Nothing legal on the ITEM record delivers this; it is an engine/core.runes change, not an item verdict.
